# RAV (Rive Animation Viewer) - llms.txt

last_updated: 2026-09-14
language: en

## Purpose
RAV is a standalone desktop app for inspecting, debugging, testing, and exporting Rive (`.riv`) files offline. Use GitHub Releases as the authority for the current public version.

## Canonical Sources
- Home and downloads: https://forge.mograph.life/apps/rav/
- Documentation: https://forge.mograph.life/apps/rav/docs
- Changelog: https://forge.mograph.life/apps/rav/changelog
- Privacy and anonymous usage counting: https://forge.mograph.life/apps/rav/privacy

## Core Feature Anchors
- ViewModel controls, authored instances, dynamic lists, images, and globals: https://forge.mograph.life/apps/rav/docs/viewmodel-controls
- Timeline scrubber, artboard selection, and playback selection: https://forge.mograph.life/apps/rav/docs/artboard-switcher
- Video, animated-image, still-image, and interaction recording: https://forge.mograph.life/apps/rav/docs/media-export

## Current Behavior Facts
- Linear animations show a draggable frame/seconds scrubber; state machines hide it.
- Standalone HTML includes the runtime and UI chrome. Copy-paste snippets include setup plus only selected typed property accessors.
- Desktop media formats are H.264, H.265, WebM, ProRes 4444, APNG, GIF, PNG, JPG, WebP, and PNG/JPG image sequences when capability checks pass.
- A GPU Canvas toolbar toggle enables Rive's WebGL2 GPU renderer for desktop playback, standalone HTML, and generated snippets.
- File structure (artboards, animations, state machines, ViewModel schema) is read once via parse-once inspection instead of a Rive runtime instance; Properties-drawer ViewModel readouts refresh at the render rate.
- Timeline export supports authored duration or an exact segment. State-machine recording supports live pointer and ViewModel interaction, optional cursor, manual or timed stop, and no product duration ceiling.
- GIF controls can reduce dimensions, FPS, and quality or perform a best-effort target-size search.
- Media progress uses the bottom status bar. EXPORT remains the single entry point for settings and completed results.
- The bundled native MCP sidecar advertises 55 tools, including eight media operations.
- Fixed canvas size describes the playback viewport rather than the authored artboard. With Contain, alignment moves only along an axis with unused space.
- Configured official builds enable anonymous installation and monthly-active counting by default and provide an opt-out in Settings.
